summary: Record r6 candidate checks for retained-snapshot VM deletion and the Core startup recovery fence. API impact: none.

guide.reason: This adds bounded implementation QA evidence and changes no operator workflow.

api.reason: The checks exercise existing authenticated VM-delete and Core startup-hook behavior; they add no endpoint or request/response contract.

roadmap.reason: The QA records candidate evidence within the existing recovery plan and does not change scope or acceptance criteria.

state.record: The existing Core managed-vms journal stores snapshot intent and settlement; the pool master's existing snapshot catalog supplies retained-snapshot deletion authority.
state.reason: The checks validate existing Core-owned state and add no durable record.

verification.method: Ran both authenticated VM-delete choices through a fresh disposable Controller against a retained-snapshot VM, comparing Controller and Core state before and after each terminal refusal. Invoked the r6 storage-guard CLI using inactive XML and an isolated, mode-0600 derived unresolved-intent journal, then verified the source Core journal was unchanged. The CLI fixture does not invoke libvirt start.
checks: Authenticated Controller delete with disk deletion disabled reached terminal retained-snapshot refusal; Core and Controller state unchanged — passed
Authenticated Controller delete with disk deletion enabled reached terminal retained-snapshot refusal; Core and Controller state unchanged — passed
r6 storage-guard isolated unresolved local-intent fixture returned the expected refusal; source journal unchanged — passed
go test ./internal/vmhost -run 'TestStorageGuard(RefusesUnresolvedSnapshotStateBeforeManagedVMStart|AllowsSettledSnapshotIntent)$' -count=1 — passed (see linked code assessment)
